fields.features_heading: What Goes Behind the One Link in Your Profile
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page your profile links to, the table each button reads from, and what happens after a visitor taps.
fields.feature_1:
A whole page from one sentence

Describe the buttons, the order, and the forms, and Emergent builds the page with its database. When the plan changes, a second prompt adds a button or rewrites the headline.
fields.feature_2:
Buttons that read from a table

Ask for a button whose label and address come from a row, such as today's stop or this week's event. Staff change the row, and the button shows the new value to the next visitor.
fields.feature_3:
Visits counted per profile

Give each profile its own address for the same page, and the app saves every visit with the profile it came from. Sort the rows by month to see which profile is worth posting on.
fields.feature_4:
A form on the page itself

Put a signup or inquiry form under the buttons so visitors stay on the page. Emergent can build it as one question per screen, and each answer lands in a database you own.
fields.feature_5:
Inquiries sent to the right person

Write a rule in the prompt, such as a party of 20 guests or more, and the app sends an email or Slack alert to the person who handles it, with the guest's answers in the message.
fields.feature_6:
Your own address in every bio

Publish the page on a custom domain (custom domains use credits), and the link in each bio reads as your own name. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Link in Bio Landing Page Examples
fields.tab_content_1:
Today's parking spot is always button one

Brasa Norte parks somewhere different each weekday. The first button on its link in bio landing page reads from a table the owner edits each morning. On Tuesday the row says Harbor and 5th, 11 am to 2 pm, and the button shows exactly that. The menu and catering links sit below it and stay put.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every visit is counted by the profile that sent it

Larkspur Lane Books posts on three platforms, and each profile links to the page through a different address. The app tags every visit with its profile and saves it as a row. Of last month's 2,400 visits, the TikTok profile sent 1,300, the YouTube channel 700, and the Pinterest board 400.
fields.tab_content_3:
An inquiry for 20 or more guests goes to the events manager

Bar staff at Copperline Taproom keep the tap list in a table that feeds the page. Below it, a private party form asks for the date and the head count. An inquiry for 20 or more guests, such as the Marlow birthday for 24, is emailed to events manager Ines Calloway. Smaller groups go to the front-of-house inbox.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each dog marked adopted drops off the list

Hollow Pine Animal Rescue tracks its adoptable dogs in a table, and a card for each of the 14 listed this week appears on the page. When staff mark a dog adopted, as they did for Biscuit, its card leaves the page. A volunteer signup at the bottom saves each name to the volunteers table.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Link in Bio Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a link in bio landing page from a list of profiles to a tested page with its address in every bio.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose the one link that leads
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep changing links in a table
fields.howto_step_1_des: List each profile the page will sit behind, from the shop's video account to the founder's channel. Note what a visitor from each one came for, because a follower who found you through a recipe video wants something different from a wholesale buyer.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the single thing you want visitors to do this week, such as finding the truck or claiming a seat, and make it the first button. Put everything else below it in order of how often people ask for it, and cut what nobody asks for.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent what each button does, which forms sit on the page, and who hears about each answer. Emergent builds the page and its database from that prompt. A follow-up prompt reorders the buttons or adds a new one later.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Anything that changes weekly, such as today's location or this month's event, belongs in a table row, not in the page itself. Ask for that button to read its label and address from the row, then hand the table to whoever updates it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Size every button for a thumb
fields.howto_step_5_des: Google's Android accessibility guidance suggests touch targets of at least 48x48dp, separated by 8dp of space or more. Use that as the floor for every button, keep labels to a few words, and check that the first button shows without scrolling.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the published page from every profile on a phone, tap each button, and submit one test entry per form. Check that each visit lands as a row with the right profile and that each alert reaches the person it names.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Paste the address into every bio
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the page's address to each profile, using the address you gave that profile. Once a month, sort the visits by profile and by button, move the busiest button up, and retire any link nobody has tapped.

faq_plan.q: What is a link in bio landing page?
faq_plan.a: A link in bio landing page is a single page, built for a phone screen, that the link in a social profile points to. It holds the buttons, forms, and lists a follower might want next. One address then serves every post you publish.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a link in bio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write a prompt for Emergent's AI landing page builder that lists the buttons in the order you want them and any form the page should carry. Emergent builds the page from it. Publish it, paste the address into each profile's bio, and tap through it once on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Which link should sit at the top of a link in bio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put the one action you want this week at the top, such as a new product or an event signup. Below it, add answers to what followers keep asking in comments and messages: where to buy, when you are open, how to book. Leave off links to the profiles visitors already came from.

faq_plan.q: When is a list of links the wrong choice for a bio landing page?
faq_plan.a: A list is the wrong choice when visitors come to make one decision about you. If people arrive to learn who you are and hire you, a personal landing page with one next step does that job better than six buttons. Keep the list for accounts that post about several things at once.

faq_plan.q: How many buttons should a link in bio landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Start with four or fewer, and add one only when followers ask for something the page does not answer. Every button past the first competes with it for the same tap. Count taps per button for a month, then drop the one at the bottom.

faq_plan.q: Can a link in bio landing page have an address under my name?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Connect one, and the address in each bio sits under your own name. Pick something short enough to read off a video or say out loud, because some followers will type it in by hand.

faq_plan.q: Can I show work samples on a link in bio landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but keep them small: two or three thumbnails that each open the full piece. For a body of work a client will study, point one button to a portfolio landing page and let the bio page stay a quick router to everything else.

faq_plan.q: How do I see which buttons on a link in bio landing page get tapped?
faq_plan.a: Ask for it in the prompt: save each tap as a row with the button name and the time, and show a weekly count per button. The rows sit in a database you own. Sort them by button or by week to find the links that never get a tap.

faq_plan.q: Does a link in bio landing page cost anything to publish?
faq_plan.a: It does not have to. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Publish a first version with two buttons, then add more once you can see where the taps go.

faq_plan.q: What should my link in bio landing page show during a launch?
faq_plan.a: Move the launch to the first button for as long as the launch runs, and point it to a page of its own. A product launch landing page can carry the full pitch and the signup, while the bio page stays short. When the launch ends, move that button back down.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this keyword is listicles of link-in-bio tools, a few tutorials and template galleries; each treats the page as a static list of buttons. This page shows the link in bio landing page as a small app built from a prompt: buttons that read from a table the owner edits, one page shared by several profiles and counted per profile, inquiries routed by a rule, and a list that drops items when staff mark them done. The FAQ covers the definition, building it, what links belong on it, how many, a link page versus a page about one person, using your own domain, work samples, click counts, building it free, and launches.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Link in Bio Landing Page for Every Profile You Run'; every section stays on the page a profile link points to.

intent.evidence: Definition first in FAQ 1 ('a single page, built for a phone screen, that the link in a social profile points to'), four examples, a seven-step how-to, a comparison table; matches the link-in-bio tool SERP.

specificity.evidence: 'On Tuesday the row says Harbor and 5th, 11 am to 2 pm'; 'Of last month's 2,400 visits, the TikTok profile sent 1,300'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on actions: 'Describe the buttons, the order, and the forms'; 'Ask for a button whose label and address come from a row'.

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings; QC Q-codes clear. feature_5 37-word sentence accepted as P2.

voice.evidence: 'a follower who found you through a recipe video wants something different from a wholesale buyer' reads as an operator.

truth.evidence: Claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts ('email or Slack alert'), conversational ('one question per screen'), custom-domain ('use credits'), code-export ('On paid plans'), free-start. Step 5 keeps the source's scope: 'Google's Android accessibility guidance suggests touch targets of at least 48x48dp, separated by 8dp of space or more' vs source 'Consider making touch targets at least 48x48dp, separated by 8dp of space or more'.

distinct.evidence: Examples are a taco truck, bookshop (TikTok/YouTube/Pinterest, not Instagram), taproom and rescue: no creator, artist or influencer case. FAQ 4 and FAQ 7 route personal and portfolio intent to those siblings ('a personal landing page with one next step does that job better'; 'point one button to a portfolio landing page'). No sibling primary in a heading (QC K clear).

faq.evidence: 10 items, hub link in FAQ 2 ('Emergent's AI landing page builder'), each answer answers its question in the first sentence.

images.evidence: Tab 2 draws 1,300 + 700 + 400 = 2,400; tab 3 Marlow birthday 24 to Ines Calloway; tab 4 '14 Listed this week', 'Biscuit marked adopted', 'Card removed from the page'. The Biscuit 'Adopted' chip is the staff table row, the outcome card shows the removal: no contradiction on names, numbers or outcome.

findings.issue: The main panel is headed like the public page ('Adoptable dogs', '14 Listed this week') while it shows Biscuit with an 'Adopted' chip, so a quick reader may think the adopted dog is still on the page. The copy says the dogs live in a table and the hero card says 'Card removed from the page', so the story holds; the panel label is just ambiguous.
findings.fix: If re-rendered for another reason, title the panel 'Dogs table' so it reads as the staff record.

findings.issue: QC Q9: 'profile' (22), 'button' (18) and 'table' (10) recur heavily; the how-to steps 1, 6 and 7 all turn on 'each profile'.
findings.fix: Vary with 'account', 'channel', 'link' where the meaning allows.
